miniProject.title: Atomic sharded checkpoints with kill-tested recovery
miniProject.brief: Extend trainlab `ckpt/` and `faults/` with sharded DCP checkpoints, manifests, atomic publish and changed-layout restore. Prove recovery with kill-at-every-boundary campaigns, corruption refusal and a per-incident audit trail, so restarts resume the same experiment instead of a shifted one.
steps: Port the DCP recipe to CPU `gloo`: save a sharded model plus optimizer state through `get_state_dict`, reload bit-exactly after mutation, convert to a single file, and resume sampler position with RNG streams intact.
Add versioned manifests with topology, config and code identity plus strict-versus-lax key policy, and pass the TorchTitan CPU checkpoint suite with every refusal and remap logged.

Publish through a temporary directory with barrier discipline, manifest-last commit and per-shard checksums; corrupt one byte to prove refusal, and keep retention that never deletes the last known good.

Coordinate one outstanding asynchronous save, adding the `DefaultStager` variant for staging-before-step discipline, and time it against synchronous saves on CPU, then work the MLSys checkpoint-tax boxes to set interval, RPO and RTO.

Restore a sharded checkpoint onto a changed world size with full-parameter equality, then rehearse the Stas preemption trap and a bounded crash restart under the elastic-run reference from global step.
List every kill window in the save and load cycle from the code, kill in each one, and show every kill resumes to the reference trajectory or refuses loudly with a manifest and audit entry.
deliverables: The `ckpt/` sharded save, manifest, atomic publish and changed-layout restore with refusal tests.
Sync-versus-async timings, the interval derivation with RPO and RTO, and retention plus watchdog evidence.
The kill campaign matrix with reference-trajectory results and the per-incident failure manifest plus recovery audit.

checks.name: PyTorch asynchronous checkpoint recipe
checks.note: Port the async loop with one outstanding request and separated staging discipline.

checks.name: TorchTitan CPU checkpoint suite
checks.note: Run the save, load, selection and purge cases on CPU; keep the suite green.

checks.name: MLSys Checkpoint 1.4 boxes
checks.note: Work the interval and tax boxes on paper before setting the job policy.

checks.name: Stas fault-tolerance guide
checks.note: Rehearse the preemption trap and retention arithmetic on a CPU job.

checks.name: PyTorch elastic run reference
checks.note: Run the bounded-restart test and crash loop on CPU gloo.

rubric.pass: Mid-epoch resume reproduces batches, RNG draws and weights exactly on CPU, with every stream named.
rubric.strong: Dropping any single stream fails a named test, and cross-size restore keeps moments aligned.

rubric.pass: Interrupted publishes never appear on the load path, and tampered shards are refused by checksum with fallback kept.
rubric.strong: Retention holds the last known good under corruption, and the watchdog names byte rate and headroom.

rubric.pass: Every kill window is tested, each kill resumes to the trajectory or refuses with an audit entry.
rubric.strong: The audit names kept and refused artifacts per incident, and preemption exits inside a derived budget.

miniProject.feedsInto: Sharded checkpoints, the restore mesh and the kill campaign feed fleet runbooks, the extension baseline and the capstone dossier.
